title: Upper & lower limb theory · 19 January 2022 (filename)
note: The downloaded filename supplies 19 January 2022; the body identifies an upper/lower anatomy paper but does not independently print the sitting date. Q1–20 lower limb; Q21–45 upper limb.

questions.prompt: ؟ The anterolateral wall of the adductor chanal is formed by which of the following
questions.note: Vastus medialis forms the anterolateral wall of the adductor canal.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the following muscles receive nerve from the medial plantar nerve except ..
questions.note: Flexor accessorius (quadratus plantae) is lateral plantar-supplied; the other three are medial plantar-supplied.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the following are part of the ilium bone except
questions.note: The pectineal line is on the pubis, whereas arcuate and gluteal lines are on the ilium.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: ؟Which bone is the smallest bone in the Tarsal region
questions.note: Intermediate cuneiform is the smallest tarsal bone.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the following arteries are involved in the formation of cruciate anastomosis except
questions.note: Cruciate anastomosis involves circumflex femoral transverse branches, inferior gluteal and first perforating; not descending genicular.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The gluteus maximus muscle is attached to all the following parts except ..
questions.note: Gluteus maximus attaches to posterior ilium, sacrum/coccyx and sacrotuberous ligament, inserting on femur and IT tract; not pubis.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: ؟ Acetabular artery is branches from which of the following arteries
questions.note: The usual acetabular branch is obturator-derived, absent from these choices. Medial circumflex femoral can give an acetabular contribution and is the defensible listed answer, not the usual dominant route.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: which of the following nerves is going to innervate inferior cutaneous surface of gluteal region?
options: Branches from posterior cutaneous of thigh
questions.note: Inferior cluneal branches of posterior femoral cutaneous supply lower buttock skin.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All the following arteries originate from the posterior tibia except ..?
questions.note: Posterior tibial recurrent is usually an anterior tibial branch, arising before the artery crosses the interosseous membrane.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the following muscles attached to greater trochanter of femur except
questions.note: Adductor brevis inserts on the pectineal line/proximal linea aspera, not greater trochanter.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: In the case of the saphenous nerve, all of the following are true except .
options: It is the thickest cutaneous branch of the femoral nerve
It has a branch that participates in the sub-sartorial network
questions.note: Saphenous is sensory; tensor fasciae latae is supplied by superior gluteal nerve.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which of the following muscles is attached to the cuboid bone?
questions.note: Flexor hallucis brevis arises in part from plantar cuboid/lateral cuneiform and tibialis posterior expansion.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the following muscles attached to calcaneous except..?
questions.note: The second lumbrical arises from adjacent long-flexor tendons, not calcaneus.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: There are all the following sides on body of the tibia except ..
questions.note: Interpreting “sides” as surfaces, anterior is a border, not a named tibial shaft surface. The supplied posterior answer is incorrect.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the following arteries are branches of the femoral artery except ...
questions.note: Superior lateral genicular arises from popliteal artery.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: In which bone is Sustantaculum talli found?
questions.note: Sustentaculum tali is a medial calcaneal projection.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which muscle forms the oblique popliteal ligament?
questions.note: Semimembranosus expansion forms the oblique popliteal ligament.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Where is the soleus line found in the tibia?
questions.note: Soleal line is on the posterior tibial surface.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the following elements pass through the large sciatic foramen except ..
questions.note: Obturator internus tendon exits through the lesser sciatic foramen.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the following muscles are connected to the tibia except
questions.note: EHL arises from fibula/interosseous membrane rather than tibia.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The insertion of latissimus dorsi in the arm is into the:
options: posterior border of the proximal humerus
medial lip of the intertubecular groove
lateral lip of the intertubecular groove
questions.note: Latissimus dorsi inserts into the intertubercular groove floor.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All the following arise from the common extensor origin EXCEPT:
questions.note: ECRL originates from lateral supracondylar ridge, not the common extensor origin.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which of the following pierce the medial intermuscular septum of the arm?
options: medial cutaneous nerve of the arm
questions.note: Ulnar nerve pierces the medial intermuscular septum to reach the posterior arm.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The superficial branch of the ulnar nerve supplies:
questions.note: Superficial ulnar branch supplies palmaris brevis.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: A high ulnar nerve injury might produce:
options: weak abduction of the index finger
questions.note: High ulnar injury weakens index abduction. Clawing can also occur, although it is less marked than with a distal lesion (ulnar paradox). Both A and D are accepted for this broad stem.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The surgical neck of humerus is related to the:
questions.note: Axillary nerve winds around the surgical neck.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The quadrangular space between teres major and subscapularis transmits:
questions.note: Posterior circumflex humeral artery traverses the quadrangular space. The supplied axillary-artery mark is corrected.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which of the following is INCORRECT? The biceps:
options: is paralysed by an injury to the posterior cord of the brachial plexus
is a weak flexor of the shoulder
is a powerful flexor of the elbow
questions.note: Biceps is musculocutaneous/lateral-cord supplied, not posterior-cord supplied.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which is true?
options: the pisiform bone is the first bone of the carpus to ossify
the flexor synovial sheath is only continuous from wrist to distal phalanx in the thumb
the capitate bone within the carpus is the last of these to ossify
the medial cutaneous nerve is the smallest nerve branch of the brachial plexus
questions.note: The medial cutaneous nerve of arm is commonly described as the smallest named plexus branch. The source’s B is false as worded: the little finger sheath can also communicate with the ulnar bursa. D is accepted with that anatomical qualification.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Radial nerve innervated all of the following muscles Except:
questions.note: Pronator teres is supplied by median nerve.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Following muscles produce elevation of scapula EXCEPT :
questions.note: Serratus anterior chiefly protracts and upwardly rotates; upper trapezius, rhomboids and levator elevate.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: What structure does NOT pierce the clavipectoral fascia?
questions.note: Lateral thoracic artery does not pierce the clavipectoral fascia.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The median nerve goes through the heads of which muscle?
questions.note: Median nerve passes between the two heads of pronator teres.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Brachialis is supplied by:
questions.note: Brachialis usually has musculocutaneous and a radial contribution.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Branches of the axillary artery DO NOT include:
questions.note: There is no standard medial thoracic branch of the axillary artery.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The superficial branch of the ulnar nerve supplies:
questions.note: Palmaris brevis receives the superficial ulnar branch.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Extensor pollicis longus – which is INCORRECT?
options: origin = ulnar just distal to adductor pollicis longus
insertion = base of first distal phalanx
questions.note: EPL forms the ulnar/medial boundary of the snuffbox. B also contains a printing defect (“adductor” for abductor pollicis longus), so A and B are accepted without silently repairing the source.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which of the following structures IS NOT one of the contents of the carpal tunnel?
questions.note: Ulnar artery passes superficial to the flexor retinaculum in Guyon canal, not through the carpal tunnel.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which carpal bone is most commonly dislocated?
questions.note: Lunate is the classically most commonly dislocated carpal; scaphoid is most commonly fractured.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: In the forearm:
options: the radial artery lies lateral to the radial nerve in the middle third
the anterior interosseous nerve arises from the radial nerve
the posterior interosseous nerve passes between the two layers of the supinator
the brachial artery lies medial to the median nerve in the cubital fossa
questions.note: Posterior interosseous nerve traverses supinator. The superficial radial nerve lies lateral to radial artery in the middle forearm.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: A 45-year-old man is unable to initiate abduction of the arm following reduction of a dislocated shoulder. Damage to which nerve is most likely to be responsible for this condition:
questions.note: Suprascapular nerve supplies supraspinatus, which initiates abduction.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the following muscles attach to dorsal digital expanstion Except?
questions.note: Long abductor of the thumb inserts mainly at first metacarpal, unlike finger lumbricals and interossei attaching to expansions.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which muscle arises from both the radius and ulna:
questions.note: APL originates from posterior radius, ulna and interosseous membrane.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: In the cubital fossa:
options: the medial wall is formed by pronator teres
the floor is formed mainly by the supinator
the radial nerve lies medial to the biceps tendon
questions.note: Pronator teres forms the medial boundary. The floor includes brachialis and supinator.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: As it emerges from the axilla, the median nerve lies where with regards to the brachial artery?
questions.note: Median nerve initially lies lateral to brachial artery, then crosses to become medial.
questions.subject: anatomy
